raw_results.question: Count how many triangles do stations named Hatton Cross, and Green Park participate in. Give final answer in the format station: answer. Separate answers with comma. Do not output anything else.

parameters.query:
MATCH (s:UndergroundStation) WHERE s.name IN ['Hatton Cross','Green Park']
OPTIONAL MATCH (s)--(a:UndergroundStation) WHERE a<>s
WITH s, collect(DISTINCT a) AS ns
UNWIND (CASE WHEN size(ns)=0 THEN [null] ELSE ns END) AS a
UNWIND (CASE WHEN size(ns)=0 THEN [null] ELSE ns END) AS b
WITH s, a, b WHERE a IS NOT NULL AND b IS NOT NULL AND elementId(a)<elementId(b) AND EXISTS((a)--(b))
RETURN s.name, count(*) AS triangles

parameters.query: MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Covent Garden'}) CALL gds.allShortestPaths.delta.stream('tube', {sourceNode: s, relationshipWeightProperty:'time', delta:50}) YIELD index, targetNode, totalCost, nodeIds, costs RETURN [n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name] AS path, costs ORDER BY index

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Covent Garden'}) CALL gds.allShortestPaths.delta.stream('tube', {sourceNode: s, relationshipWeightProperty:'time', delta:50}) YIELD index, nodeIds, costs WITH collect([n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name] AS p, costs AS c) AS x RETURN size(x) AS n

raw_results.question: I would like to use the Dijkstra single-source shortest path to find all paths from Arsenal, using distance as the weight. Provide the paths with costs as answers. The example format is: ["Holloway Road", "X"]: [0.0, 42.0], ["Holloway Road", "B", "C"]: [0.0, 9.5, 9.6].

parameters.cypher_query: MATCH (n:UndergroundStation)-[r:LINK]->(m:UndergroundStation) RETURN gds.graph.project($graph_name, n, m, {sourceNodeLabels: labels(n), targetNodeLabels: labels(m), relationshipType: type(r), relationshipProperties: {distance: toFloat(r.distance)}})

parameters.query: MATCH (a:UndergroundStation)-[r:LINK]->(b:UndergroundStation) RETURN a.name AS a, b.name AS b, min(r.distance) AS d

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'}) CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('g',{sourceNode:s, relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'}) YIELD nodeIds, costs RETURN [n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name] AS p, costs ORDER BY size(p), costs[-1]

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'}) CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('g',{sourceNode:s, relationshipTypes:['LINK'], relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'}) YIELD nodeIds, costs RETURN [n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name] AS p, costs ORDER BY size(p), costs[-1]

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'}) CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('g',{sourceNode:s, relationshipTypes:['LINK'], relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'}) YIELD nodeIds, costs WITH [n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name] AS p, costs ORDER BY size(p), costs[-1], p SKIP 0 LIMIT 110 RETURN apoc.text.join([x IN p | '"'+x+'"'], ', ') AS path, costs

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'}) CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('g',{sourceNode:s, relationshipTypes:['LINK'], relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'}) YIELD nodeIds, costs WITH [n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name] AS p, costs ORDER BY size(p), costs[-1], p SKIP 0 LIMIT 100 RETURN '[' + reduce(a='', x IN p | a + CASE WHEN a='' THEN '' ELSE ', ' END + '"' + x + '"') + ']: [' + reduce(a='', c IN costs | a + CASE WHEN a='' THEN '' ELSE ', ' END + toString(c)) + ']' AS r

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'}) CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('g',{sourceNode:s, relationshipTypes:['LINK'], relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'}) YIELD nodeIds, costs WITH [n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name] AS p, costs ORDER BY size(p), costs[-1], p SKIP 100 LIMIT 100 RETURN '[' + reduce(a='', x IN p | a + CASE WHEN a='' THEN '' ELSE ', ' END + '"' + x + '"') + ']: [' + reduce(a='', c IN costs | a + CASE WHEN a='' THEN '' ELSE ', ' END + toString(c)) + ']' AS r

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'}) CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('g',{sourceNode:s, relationshipTypes:['LINK'], relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'}) YIELD nodeIds, costs WITH [n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name] AS p, costs ORDER BY size(p), costs[-1], p SKIP 200 LIMIT 110 RETURN '[' + reduce(a='', x IN p | a + CASE WHEN a='' THEN '' ELSE ', ' END + '"' + x + '"') + ']: [' + reduce(a='', c IN costs | a + CASE WHEN a='' THEN '' ELSE ', ' END + toString(c)) + ']' AS r

raw_results.question: I would like to find the minimum weighted spanning tree rooted at Hammersmith using time as the relationship weight. I want the output to be in the format of a sequence of [node, parent, weight]. For example: ["A", "B", 2.0], ["A", "C", 3.0], ["K", "L", 9.5].

parameters.query: MATCH (n:UndergroundStation) WHERE n.name CONTAINS 'Hammersmith' RETURN n.name, n.id

parameters.cypher_query:
MATCH (n:UndergroundStation)-[r:LINK]->(m:UndergroundStation)
RETURN gds.graph.project($graph_name, n, m, {sourceNodeLabels: labels(n), targetNodeLabels: labels(m), sourceNodeProperties: {}, targetNodeProperties: {}, relationshipType: type(r), relationshipProperties: {time: toFloat(r.time)}}, {undirectedRelationshipTypes: ['LINK']})

I did not check the two edge lists against each other row by row. Ties between equal-weight edges can be broken differently by different runs, but the total weight is the same.

response_data.final_result:
I couldn't get a longest path to Notting Hill Gate. The GDS `longest_path` algorithm only works on directed acyclic graphs, and this graph isn't one.

- I projected all 302 `UndergroundStation` nodes and 812 `LINK` relationships, weighted by `distance`, and ran `longest_path` with Notting Hill Gate as the target. It returned "No longest paths found", which the tool gives when the graph contains cycles.
- A Cypher check confirms the cause. All 812 links have a reverse link between the same two stations, so every pair of connected stations forms a cycle.
- I dropped the projection afterwards.

I didn't make up a path or pick an arbitrary way to turn this into a DAG. Any such choice would change the answer.

I can try one of these instead:
1. Use a different notion of "longest": the longest simple path, which is NP-hard and would have to be bounded or approximated, or the longest shortest path (the farthest station from Notting Hill Gate by weighted distance, using Dijkstra).
2. Make the graph a DAG, for example by keeping only links that go one way along each line, and then run `longest_path`. The result depends on which direction I keep.

Which would you like, and should the cost be `distance` or `time`?

parameters.query: MATCH (n:UndergroundStation) WHERE n.name CONTAINS 'Westminster' OR n.name CONTAINS 'Waterloo' RETURN n.name

MATCH (a:UndergroundStation) WHERE a.name IN ['Westminster','Waterloo'] MATCH (b:UndergroundStation) WHERE b<>a MATCH p=shortestPath((a)-[:LINK*]-(b)) WITH a, sum(1.0/length(p)) AS s RETURN a.name, s/301 AS harmonic

parameters.query: MATCH (a:UndergroundStation {name:'Westminster'}), (b:UndergroundStation) WHERE a<>b MATCH p=shortestPath((a)-[:LINK*]-(b)) WITH count(b) AS c, sum(length(p)) AS s RETURN c, s, toFloat(c)/s AS cl, (toFloat(c)/301)*(toFloat(c)/s) AS wf

Canada Water's eigenvector centrality is **0.00061**, using GDS defaults (20 iterations, default L2 normalization). That score is very close to zero and isn't a converged value, so I wouldn't treat it as meaningful.

I projected all 302 `UndergroundStation` nodes and the `LINK` relationships as an undirected, unweighted graph (1,624 relationships) and ran the algorithm in stream mode.

- **Score depends on iterations:** With max-scaling at 20 iterations, Canada Water scores 0.001234, against 0.402583 for Baker Street and 0.172966 for Bank. Run to convergence (144 iterations, `did_converge=True`), Canada Water drops to 0.0.

- **Likely cause:** I didn't confirm it, but the principal eigenvector appears to concentrate on a small, dense part of the network, so most stations tend to 0 as iterations increase.

The robust conclusion is that Canada Water is a low-centrality station on this measure, far below Baker Street and Bank. I haven't cross-checked the exact value with a different method, so don't rely on 0.00061 as a precise figure. If you need a stable ranking, PageRank or degree centrality would suit this graph better.

parameters.query:
MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'})
CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('tube', {sourceNode: s, relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'})
YIELD targetNode, totalCost, nodeIds, costs
RETURN [n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name] AS p, costs AS c ORDER BY totalCost, size(nodeIds)

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'})
CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('tube', {sourceNode: s, relationshipTypes:['LINK'], relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'})
YIELD targetNode, totalCost, nodeIds, costs
RETURN [n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name] AS p, costs AS c ORDER BY totalCost, size(nodeIds)

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'})
CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('tube', {sourceNode: s, relationshipTypes:['LINK'], relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'})
YIELD targetNode, totalCost, nodeIds, costs
WITH totalCost, nodeIds, costs ORDER BY totalCost, size(nodeIds), nodeIds SKIP 0 LIMIT 100
RETURN apoc.text.join([n IN nodeIds | gds.util.asNode(n).name],'>')+' '+apoc.text.join([c IN costs | toString(c)],',') AS r

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'})
CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('tube', {sourceNode: s, relationshipTypes:['LINK'], relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'})
YIELD targetNode, totalCost, nodeIds, costs
WITH totalCost, nodeIds, costs ORDER BY totalCost, size(nodeIds), nodeIds
WITH collect([nodeIds,costs]) AS all
UNWIND range(0,size(all)-1) AS i
WITH i, all[i] AS x WHERE i < 150
RETURN reduce(a='', n IN x[0] | a + CASE WHEN a='' THEN '' ELSE '|' END + gds.util.asNode(n).name) + ' ' + reduce(b='', c IN x[1] | b + CASE WHEN b='' THEN '' ELSE ',' END + toString(c)) AS r

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'})
CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('tube', {sourceNode: s, relationshipTypes:['LINK'], relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'})
YIELD targetNode, totalCost, nodeIds, costs
WITH totalCost, nodeIds, costs ORDER BY totalCost, size(nodeIds), nodeIds
WITH collect([nodeIds,costs]) AS rows
UNWIND range(0,size(rows)-1) AS i
WITH i, rows[i] AS x WHERE i < 150
RETURN reduce(a='', n IN x[0] | a + CASE WHEN a='' THEN '' ELSE '|' END + gds.util.asNode(n).name) + ' ' + reduce(b='', c IN x[1] | b + CASE WHEN b='' THEN '' ELSE ',' END + toString(c)) AS r

MATCH (s:UndergroundStation {name:'Arsenal'})
CALL gds.allShortestPaths.dijkstra.stream('tube', {sourceNode: s, relationshipTypes:['LINK'], relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'})
YIELD targetNode, totalCost, nodeIds, costs

raw_results.question: Compute the minimum directed Steiner tree starting from Bank and spanning the terminals Waterloo, Southwark, and Westminster. I want the output to be in the format of a sequence of [node, parent, weight]. For example: ["A", "B", 2.0], ["A", "C", 3.0], ["K", "L", 9.5].

parameters.cypher_query: MATCH (n:UndergroundStation)-[r:LINK]->(m:UndergroundStation) RETURN gds.graph.project($graph_name, n, m, {sourceNodeLabels: labels(n), targetNodeLabels: labels(m), relationshipType: type(r), relationshipProperties: {distance: toFloat(r.distance)}})

response_data.final_result:
The minimum directed Steiner tree from Bank to Waterloo, Southwark and Westminster has a total weight of 7.0, using the `distance` property on `LINK` as the weight:

["Waterloo", "Bank", 4.0], ["Westminster", "Waterloo", 2.0], ["Southwark", "Waterloo", 1.0]

I used `distance` because the question didn't say which weight to use. raw_results.question: Compute the prize-collecting Steiner tree on the database graph, using distance as the relationship weight and zone as the node prize. Format the results as a sequence of [node, parent, weight]. For example: ["A", "B", 2.0], ["A", "C", 3.0], ["K", "L", 9.5].

parameters.cypher_query:
MATCH (n:UndergroundStation)-[r:LINK]->(m:UndergroundStation)
RETURN gds.graph.project($graph_name, n, m, {sourceNodeLabels: labels(n), targetNodeLabels: labels(m), sourceNodeProperties: {zone: toFloat(n.zone)}, targetNodeProperties: {zone: toFloat(m.zone)}, relationshipType: type(r), relationshipProperties: {distance: toFloat(r.distance)}}, {undirectedRelationshipTypes: ['LINK']})

parameters.query:
CALL gds.prizeCollectingSteinerTree.stream('pcst', {prizeProperty:'zone', relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'}) YIELD nodeId, parentId, weight
RETURN collect([gds.util.asNode(nodeId).name, gds.util.asNode(parentId).name, weight]) AS edges, count(*) AS n, sum(weight) AS total

CALL gds.alpha.pcst.stream('pcst', {prizeProperty:'zone', relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'}) YIELD nodeId, parentId, weight
RETURN collect([gds.util.asNode(nodeId).name, gds.util.asNode(parentId).name, weight]) AS edges, count(*) AS n, sum(weight) AS total
SHOW PROCEDURES YIELD name WHERE toLower(name) CONTAINS 'steiner' OR toLower(name) CONTAINS 'pcst' OR toLower(name) CONTAINS 'prize' RETURN name

CALL gds.prizeSteinerTree.stream('pcst', {prizeProperty:'zone', relationshipWeightProperty:'distance'}) YIELD nodeId, parentId, weight

raw_results.question: What are the five stations located nearest to Paddington? List the station names in the format ["A", "B", "C"].

parameters.query: MATCH (p:UndergroundStation) WHERE p.name CONTAINS 'Paddington' WITH collect(p) AS ps UNWIND ps AS p MATCH (s:UndergroundStation) WHERE NOT s.name CONTAINS 'Paddington' RETURN p.name AS pname, s.name AS name, point.distance(point({latitude:p.latitude,longitude:p.longitude}), point({latitude:s.latitude,longitude:s.longitude})) AS d ORDER BY pname, d LIMIT 12
